headline: Over 50 blasts, 8 buses torched in Dhaka as violence erupts
summary: A school bus was set on fire in Bhatara while crude bombs exploded across the city, including near the CID headquarters and Dhaka University.
details: Miscreants set fire to a school bus belonging to Jalsiri Cantonment School and College in the Bhatara area of the capital. A video of the incident shows the yellow bus engulfed in flames while parked on the roadside.
Simultaneously, crude bomb explosions were reported at several locations across Dhaka. These included the area around Dhaka University, where three people were detained by security forces.
Other targeted locations included the front of the Pallabi police station, Sony Hall in Mirpur-1, and the CID headquarters in Malibagh.
Reports indicate that over 50 blasts occurred in total, with eight buses being torched across the city as part of the sóng of violence.
caption:
Over 50 blasts and 8 buses torched. Dhaka is under attack.

Miscreants set fire to a school bus belonging to Jalsiri Cantonment School and College in the Bhatara area of the capital. A video of the incident shows the yellow bus engulfed in flames while parked on the roadside.

Simultaneously, crude bomb explosions were reported at several locations across Dhaka. These included the area around Dhaka University, where three people were detained by security forces.

Other targeted locations included the front of the Pallabi police station, Sony Hall in Mirpur-1, and the CID headquarters in Malibagh.

Reports indicate that over 50 blasts occurred in total, with eight buses being torched across the city as part of the sóng of violence.

headline_marked: 3 [[Dhaka Tribune journalists held hostage]] and tortured by drug gang in Tongi
headline: 3 Dhaka Tribune journalists held hostage and tortured by drug gang in Tongi
summary: The journalists were held at gunpoint for three hours, beaten, and forced to drink a liquid containing sleeping pills by an armed gang in Gazipur.
details: Three Dhaka Tribune journalists—reporters Rabiul Hasan and Asiful Islam Rifat, and photojournalist Abir Ahmed Supto—were attacked by armed assailants while investigating drug trafficking in Tongi, Gazipur.

The victims were held hostage for approximately three hours on Friday evening in the Haji's Mazar slum area. They report being beaten, threatened with death at gunpoint, and forced to drink a liquid mixed with sleeping pills.

A group of 20 to 25 armed men reportedly kidnapped the journalists during their information-gathering process. The assailants then filmed a video of them making false confessions with drugs and money placed in front of them.

During the incident, the gang members seized the journalists' cameras, mobile phones, and identification cards. A written complaint has been filed with the Tongi West Police Station by reporter Rabiul Hasan.

This attack follows a similar incident where a journalist from the Daily Kalbela was allegedly kidnapped and tortured in the same area, raising serious concerns over the safety of journalists in the region.
